content.intro: Learn secrets and sensitive data through a compact visual, an inspectable Django example, and a practical verification task.
content.why_it_matters: Secrets and Sensitive Data matters because a Django project has to behave predictably across requests, database state, configuration, and deployments. Understanding this piece makes the surrounding application easier to test, maintain, and secure.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: This lesson examines secrets and sensitive data as part of security and privacy. The objective is to understand the behavior, connect it to the listed subtopics, and verify it with a small example rather than relying on memorized syntax.

content_blocks.title: What to cover
content_blocks.text: The source syllabus for this lesson names: Secret-key management; Database and API credentials; Password storage; Sensitive logs; Preventing accidental disclosure through repositories and error pages. Keep these distinct concepts together: know what each item does, when it applies, and what assumption must be verified in your project.

items.title: Secret-key management
items.text: Secret-key management is a server-side responsibility where applicable. Define who may perform the action and on which object, validate untrusted input, test denied cases, and document sensitive-data handling.

items.title: Database and API credentials
items.text: An API contract specifies resources, methods, body validation, authentication, permissions, status codes, pagination, versioning and error formats. JSON transport alone does not make an API safe or complete.

items.title: Password storage
items.text: For Password storage, identify the Django component responsible, the inputs and outputs it owns, and the boundary conditions that matter. Use the accompanying example as a starting point, verify it with the official versioned documentation, and record one test demonstrating expected behavior.

items.title: Preventing accidental disclosure through repositories and error pages
items.text: Treat Preventing accidental disclosure through repositories and error pages as a reproducible diagnostic: capture the exact input and observed result, isolate one hypothesis, and add a regression test once the cause is fixed. Avoid exposing internal stack traces or secrets to public users.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Change one input or configuration choice related to Secret-key management. Write down the expected outcome, test one normal case and one invalid or boundary case, then record what changed. Do not add real credentials or sensitive production data.

content_blocks.title: Common mistakes and fixes
content_blocks.text: Common pitfalls include skipping a required configuration/import, copying a fragment without its model or URL context, trusting client input, or treating a development-only behavior as production-ready. Check the earliest failing assumption, consult the version-specific docs, and add a regression test for the failure you found.
